title: Reduce observability tail latency by refactoring exporter backpressure and upgrading OpenTelemetry stack
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement:

We continue to see occasional p99/p999 request tail latency spikes correlated with peak telemetry emission and collector backpressure. Current analysis points to blocking exporter handoffs and unbounded serializer allocations in the runtime trace/log path under load. These spikes increase request latency variance for latency-sensitive realtime serving routes and amplify user-facing slowdowns during bursty workloads.

Goal:

Reduce tail latency and allocation pressure by refactoring the in-process observability exporter pipeline to a bounded, non-blocking handoff with backpressure signals; upgrade OpenTelemetry SDK/collector components to latest stable maintenance release; and replace the heavy JSON log path with a compact protobuf/lineprotocol serialization for high-rate paths. The change should preserve sampling semantics and not increase network egress.

High-level approach:

1) Upgrade opentelemetry-go SDK and collector forwarder to the vetted 1.14.x -> 1.15.x line that contains batching and exporter deadlock fixes.
2) Introduce a bounded lock-free ring buffer handoff between instrumented code and background exporter workers (configurable size, default 16k events), with a dropped-event counter and last-drop-timestamp metric exposed.
3) Move heavy serialization (log JSON, pretty spans) off the hot path into background workers; for critical low-CPU code paths use compact protobuf line protocol for logs/traces.
4) Implement adaptive batching in exporter worker keyed by recent latency and queue fill ratio; ensure graceful flush on shutdown.
5) Add end-to-end benchmarks and flamegraphs to verify allocation drop and tail latency improvement.

Trade-offs and risks:

- Dropping or deferring telemetry when queue fills reduces observability fidelity during the highest load, but keeps serving latency bounded. We will expose drop metrics and tune queue sizes based on real traffic.
- Upgrading OTEL introduces surface-area changes; need to verify no regression for our span context propagation across network boundaries.
- Serializer format change requires collector compatibility; we'll keep a compatibility layer and gated rollout.

Rollout plan:

- Implement feature-gated exporter in runtime binary; default behavior remains current exporter.
- Canary: enable for 5% of production routing (non-critical routes) for 72h with elevated tracing retention.
- Observe drop counters, p99/p999 latency, memory, and GC pause metrics.
- If green, ramp to 50% then 100% in 48h increments.
- Rollback: toggle feature flag off and restart worker pool (no schema migration required).

Deliverables:

- PR: backend runtime exporter refactor and OTEL dependency bumps (link below).
- Canary dashboard: p50/p95/p99/p999 latency, exporter_queue_fill, exporter_dropped_events, runtime_alloc_bytes, gc_pause_ms.
- Bench harness and flamegraphs comparing current vs new path under synthetic burst load.
- Documentation: Confluence runbook for tuning queue size and rollback steps.

Success criteria:

- p99/p999 tail latency on tagged realtime routes reduced by >=30% under identical synthetic burst test.
- Allocations per request reduced by >=25% on median and p95.
- No increase in lost traces beyond expected drops (documented) and collector receives compact payloads successfully.
- No production incidents during canary rollout.
acceptance_criteria: OTEL SDK and collector updated to specified release with changelog referenced
Non-blocking bounded handoff implemented and configurable via runtime flag
Export worker adaptive batching implemented and covered by unit tests
Benchmarks show at least 30% improvement on p99/p999 tail in synthetic tests
Canary rollout executed with dashboards monitoring queue_fill and dropped_events
implementation_steps: Create feature-flagged exporter module and unit tests (code owner: runtime-telemetry team)
Upgrade opentelemetry-go and collector images; run integration tests against staging collector
Implement ring buffer handoff and backpressure metrics, expose config via runtime config service
Add background serializer worker and protobuf/lineprotocol encoder for high-rate logs
Add adaptive batching logic with configurable thresholds and shutdown flush
Add acceptance and load tests, produce flamegraphs and allocation reports
Open PR, get design and security reviews, and land canary deployment
Monitor canary for 72h and then progressively ramp
